title: Australia Signals Need to Act on Loan Fraud Seen at A$1 Billion
content: Australia’s assistant treasurer said anti-money laundering rules and the fight against scams are a key focus amid reports that mortgage fraud at Commonwealth Bank of Australia could amount to around A$1 billion ($700 million).

title: Botswana’s Credit Rating Is Cut by S&P on Diamond Industry Woes
content: S&P Global Ratings cut Botswana’s credit score late Friday, maintaining its investment grade but citing risks to fiscal stability amid diamond industry woes. The ratings company maintained a negative outlook.

title: Zelenskiy Says Tying EU Funds to Pipepine Is ‘Blackmail’
content: President Volodymyr Zelenskiy called tying Ukraine’s access to €90 billion ($103 billion) in European Union loans to the restoration of the Druzhba pipeline “blackmail.”

title: Selecta, Majority Lenders Ask Judge to Toss Antitrust Suit
content: Selecta Group BV and a group of its bondholders asked a federal judge to dismiss a lawsuit accusing them of violating US antitrust laws as creditors made a pact among themselves to negotiate a deal with the Swiss vending machine company that favored them over others.

title: Fintech Funding Jumped 27% In 2025 With Fewer Deals But Bigger Checks
content: Global venture funding to fintech startups climbed in 2025 to its highest level in several quarters, boosted by later-stage deals, Crunchbase data shows.

title: Homebuyers are paying more for mortgage credit checks. Here’s why
content: Despite being a small part of closing costs, credit report fees have become a flashpoint in the mortgage industry.

title: Personal loans surge amid affordability struggles: It's 'the middle-class refinancing option,' expert says
content: Some borrowers are turning to personal loans to refinance credit card debt. Those loans are expected increase nearly 6% this year, TransUnion forecasts

title: Credit card debt tops $1.28 trillion — consistent with ‘K-shaped’ economic divide, New York Fed research shows
content: Collectively, Americans owe $1.28 trillion on their credit cards, according to a new report by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.

title: JPMorgan Chase reins in lending to private credit firms after marking down software loans
content: JPMorgan's move shows that the biggest U.S. bank by assets wants to get ahead of potential turbulence involving private credit loans to software companies.

title: Oaktree's Howard Marks says there's no systemic problem with private credit
content: Marks said any risk stems from the pace of expansion in direct lending, which has ballooned to a market now exceeding $1 trillion since inception around 2011.

title: Blackstone’s Gray: Market ‘noise’ fueled record redemptions from world’s largest private credit fund

title: Trump administration has scaled back oversight of student loan servicers, congressional watchdog finds
content: The Department of Education has scaled back its oversight of student loan servicers, a new report from the nonpartisan Government Accountability Office finds.

title: You can't 'borrow your way out of debt,' expert says — but more consumers are trying
content: Borrowers who struggle with high-interest debt often turn to personal loans to help pay it off, but without a change in habits debt can become a cycle.

title: Federal appeals court orders end to SAVE plan used by millions of student loan borrowers
content: A federal appeals court ordered the end to the SAVE plan, the Biden administration-era program used by millions of student loan borrowers.
